essence: All opposites shine in the consciousness-mirror: true/untrue, little/much, eternal/non-eternal, Māyā-stained/self-pure. That all, from own-grasping-consciousness-rise, form-light-natured, having known — own-experience-risen glory: Lordhood — worship. Knowing that all opposites shine in the mirror from one's own grasping consciousness = glory = Lordhood; its last word is the imperative it opened with the stance for.

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of Lordhood (viśveśvaratva); the vyabhicāri is wonder (camatkāra) at all opposites shining in the mirror from one's own grasping consciousness. The rasa is the tranquility of Lordhood — the hymn that began in anupāya ends in worship.
